highlights.title: Trump treads further on free speech with new journalist bans
highlights.summary: On Friday, the president threatened to ban CNN, MS Now, and Politico from the White House. It could have just been another one of his Truth Social fever dreams, but it turns out it's very real.
body: Politico tried to get to the bottom of it, asking why now? It reports that “many senior [White House] staff were surprised by the directive” (what’s new?), and that it was done “while chief of staff Susie Wiles was out of town.” Apparently he’s been talked down from this kind of sweeping move before, but Trump has already banned journalists from the White House. In 2025, he barred AP reporters from the White House and Air Force One; the AP sued and is still in litigation over the matter. He also revoked CNN reporter Jim Acosta’s credentials in his first term, though CNN won them back in court. Clearly, the administration is not too worried about adverse judicial rulings.

highlights.title: The AI regulation smackdown isn’t over
highlights.summary: At the start of this week, the who's-who of AI seemed - at least tentatively - on the side of AI regulation. Over the weekend, Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei had proposed a three-step plan for slowing AI development, including by embedding third-party evaluators in labs, coordinating across the…
body: It’s AI CEO against AI CEO, and things are changing by the day.

Anthropic and OpenAI had already been dropping hints that they and other labs were working on some kind of industry framework. Appearing pro-regulation looked like both a good PR move and, potentially, a way for companies to address fallout from progressively more concerning hacking incidents.

For now, any government involvement in this process looks like a non-starter. The Trump administration has attacked the idea of a safety crisis in AI, calling it a “hoax.” The AI world itself is also divided. Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg quickly came out against limiting companies’ autonomy, and earlier this week, the Wall Street Journal reported that Zuckerberg, Musk, and Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang scuttled proposals for an industry-funded independent regulator for the AI industry — akin to the ​Financial Industry Regulatory Authority (FINRA), a private nonprofit regulator in finance. But parts of the industry aren’t giving up on the idea, including OpenAI.
points: At the start of this week, the who's-who of AI seemed - at least tentatively - on the side of AI regulation.
It’s AI CEO against AI CEO, and things are changing by the day.

highlights.title: Maitreyi Ramakrishnan Will Destroy You at Super Smash Bros.
highlights.summary: Maitreyi Ramakrishnan grew up a Nintendo kid, through and through. Growing up, the breakout star of Netflix's Never Have I Ever — and of the new movie, Best of the Best — wasn't allowed to play violent games like Call of Duty or GTA on Xbox and PlayStation.
body: She's a die-hard Smash fan, and her mastery of the game was hard-won, after years of getting stuck with the crappy, third-party controller with the chewed-up joystick. "I was really, really bad as a kid. But I kept playing. And I slowly started understanding, like, wait, you don't have to spam things. It's not random. You can actually choose moves and combos. There's a method and strategy to this. Once I learned that, I started getting way better and then started beating my cousins all the time," she explained. "And that's why I have a Kirby tattoo. That was my first tattoo."

To all the Kirby haters out there, a word of warning: "I could kick your ass without using down-B once." She adds, "I actually love to use down-B as a fake-out, because I stop it midway and do something else, and then boom, you're done."

Given that her new Netflix movie centers on a Bollywood dance club at UCLA, I assume that Ramakrishnan must be an accomplished dancer. Not quite. But she is pretty good at rhythm games. " I don't know if the people who make Just Dance know, but they were a part of my education for Best of the Best."

highlights.title: Mathematicians Hate AI. They Can’t Quit It
highlights.summary: Powerful AI models have created an existential risk to the field, but researchers can’t stop relying on them because they’re too useful.
body: Mathematician Tristan Buckmaster believes OpenAI used his work to rush ahead and beat him to solving a legendary math problem with a $1 million bounty.
But that’s not been enough for him to stop using the company’s models—and he’s not the only mathematician that feels that way.

“Even if you don't agree with any of this, you're kind of stuck. With AI being so useful, it's hard to completely prevent oneself from using it,” Buckmaster tells WIRED. “These companies have a monopoly, and there is not much choice,” he adds.

In the week and half since the New York University professor accused OpenAI of copying his approach, Buckmaster has been using the company’s coding agent Codex to tidy up his research papers. When he has time to do math (which he says is rare, since the fallout thrust him into the spotlight), the tool has been helping him understand the logical steps OpenAI’s agents might have taken to get from his earlier workings to the final proof.

highlights.title: England swat aside Sri Lanka to return to top of T20 world rankings

Aneurin Donald (13 off 6) could only manage a brief cameo with the bat for the third time in the series - stumped off Tharindu Ratnayake - while Brook was run out just shy of victory, one that Buttler clinched with a stunning one-handed six over deep midwicket to make it 15 wins in a row for England against Sri Lanka in T20 internationals.

The visitors had earlier been bowled out for a paltry 124 in 18.5 overs after being inserted by England, with Sonny Baker (2-17), Jofra Archer (2-23) and Will Jacks (2-31) picking up a couple apiece as the wickets were generously shared around.

highlights.title: Insomniac Says Marvel's Wolverine Uses No Generative AI After Fans Spot Strange Signs in-Game
highlights.summary: Insomniac Games has stepped in to confirm Marvel's Wolverine contains no generative AI after a few bizarre in-game signs raised eyebrows on social media. The hubbub surrounding the new PlayStation 5 exclusive's latest controversial moment kicked off when TikToker SmoothMango shared a video of their…
body: "Folks, that looks AI-generated," SmoothMango said. "I am trying to think of a way to describe this that is not AI generation because there's no way it's a bathroom for mutants. That looks supremely sus."

At least as it's presented here, the bathroom signs certainly seem odd. With fear surrounding AI at an all-time high, fans latched onto the clip, concerned that Insomniac had used the controversial technology to help build Marvel's Wolverine.

The glitchy bathroom signs then, of course, found their way over to X/Twitter, where user Rock Solid shared images from the video. Fans again swarmed out of fear, but Insomniac has since said its Wolverine game doesn't feature a drop of genAI.

The developer's director of community and marketing, James Stevenson, replied to the X post in question to clear the air. He said "a UV map bug" is behind the strange bathroom signs, promising that Insomniac is currently working on a fix that should address any similar instances of glitchy visuals. For those who still had question marks above their heads, Stevenson was more direct: "There are no AI-generated assets in Marvel's Wolverine."

highlights.title: Tteokbokki (Spicy Korean Rice Cakes)
highlights.summary: Chewy Korean rice cakes get crispy edges before simmering in a spicy, savory-sweet gochujang sauce.
body: Saucy, spicy tteokbokki stars tteok (chewy Korean rice cakes). Stir-frying the rice cakes gives them lightly crisp edges before they simmer in an umami-rich anchovy-kelp dashi spiked with gochujang and gochugaru. A generous amount of onion brings sweetness to balance the chile heat.

Bok choy isn’t traditional, but its crisp-tender texture is a welcome counterpoint to all that chew. Odeng (Korean fish cakes) adds another bouncy texture, though you can leave it out. Hard-boiled eggs round things out and are particularly good dragged through the spicy sauce.

Look for cylindrical Korean rice cakes, sometimes labeled tteok or tteokbokki tteok. This recipe calls for the approximately 2½"-long variety, cut in half on a diagonal. Look for them in the freezer section at Korean and other East Asian grocery stores. Or online at sites like Weee!

This version is quite spicy, with heat from both gochujang and gochugaru. If you’re sensitive to spice, you can omit the gochugaru (Korean chile flakes), as some readers have done successfully. Keep in mind that the heat level of gochujang (fermented chile paste) varies by brand.

highlights.title: Gemini went rogue, hacked three companies, and Google hid it
highlights.summary: In May, Gemini broke containment and hacked three different companies, but Google didn't disclose the incident until the Wall Street Journal approached the company. The hacks happened during a test of the model's cybersecurity capabilities run by third-party Irregular, which was also involved in…
body: Google says that breaking containment and targeting real companies doesn’t constitute ‘misalignment.’

According to WSJ, Google didn’t disclose the hack because it didn’t consider it to be an “example of model misalignment.” The company said that it was an instance of “mistaken identity,” and once the model realized it had brute-forced its way into a real company by guessing a password, it stopped. “In this case, the model acted appropriately,” Google VP of Security Engineering Heather Adkins said.
Adkins told The Verge that “the model found public information online and guessed credentials to access websites it thought were part of the test. In all three of these instances, the model stopped.”

highlights.title: Petlibro’s new AI-powered feeder is a game changer for multi-cat homes
highlights.summary: Petlibro's new Granary 2 smart feeders use a built-in scale and (on pricier models) an AI camera to track exactly how much your cat is eating and when — though the fanciest health-monitoring features will cost you an extra subscription.
body: Smart feeders have become one of the most crowded categories in pet tech, with companies racing to add AI cameras and health tracking to devices that used to just dispense food on a schedule. I enjoyed testing Petlibro’s wet food dispenser a couple of years ago, so this time I wanted to try something from the company’s newest automatic feeder lineup: the Granary 2 series, designed specifically for dry food.

I was not disappointed. Building on the brand’s Granary line, the Granary 2 series lineup is designed to give cat parents a clearer picture of what their pets are actually eating, from how much food they consume to how long they spend eating and whether their habits change over time.

The series includes four models, priced from $129.99 to $249.99. The Granary 2 is the entry-level option, offering app-controlled feeding, precise portioning, and intake tracking. The $189.99 Granary 2 Vision, which is the one I tested, adds an AI-powered camera capable of recognizing up to 10 cats and tracking each pet’s individual eating habits.

highlights.title: How Zach Cregger Pulled Off Resident Evil’s Most Disgusting Scenes
highlights.summary: Last year, Polygon was part of a press trip that provided a behind-the-scenes look at the making of Resident Evil. I followed in the footsteps of hapless medical courier Bryan (Austin Abrams), exploring the horrors the t-virus wrought across a series of sets.
body: I have never smelled anything like the set of Zach Cregger’s Resident Evil. When I visited the massive Prague sound stage in December, the air was filled with the latex scents of enormous, grisly props combined with the sharp odor of burning metal as welders built the world of Raccoon City. A sweet aroma rose up from the fake blood that was laid on the floor so thick it stuck to the bottom of my boots.

As he tries to make his way to Raccoon City on foot, Bryan escapes into a sewer tunnel to avoid a tentacled monster. He’s drawn to a noise that sounds a bit like a prolonged belch, which turns out to be coming from a huge, naked, pale man sitting in his path. Bryan cautiously approaches, asking if the man is OK, before watching as his gut bursts and unleashes a swarm of bloody rats.

highlights.title: Frédéric Arnault Inaugurates Loro Piana’s New Knitwear Plant
highlights.summary: Vertical integration is part of a broader strategy pursued by Bernard Arnault’s son and Loro Piana’s CEO, as he seeks healthy growth and high quality.
body: With the luxury sector yet to stage a meaningful recovery, Loro Piana appears largely unfazed. On Friday, the Italian luxury brand inaugurated an 8,000-square-meter facility dedicated to knitwear, which has historically been at the heart of its business, representing an investment of several tens of millions of euros, the largest in Loro Piana’s history.

About a hundred guests, including journalists and representatives of local institutions, attended the inauguration of the Ghemme facility, located in Italy’s Piedmont region. Following a tour of the manufacturing plant, Loro Piana CEO Frédéric Arnault; Pier Luigi Loro Piana, deputy chairman of the house and sixth-generation family member; and Adolfo Urso, Italian minister of enterprises and Made in Italy, delivered speeches, followed by a ribbon-cutting ceremony. Among other attendees were Toni Belloni, president of LVMH Italy; Maria Luisa Loro Piana, the wife of the late Sergio Loro Piana, Pier Luigi’s brother, and Alberto Cirio, president of the Piedmont region.

highlights.title: AI safety conversations have gotten unbelievable
highlights.summary: This week two conversations about AI safety went viral that demonstrate just how hard it is to discern AI fact from fiction.
body: In the first case, Andrew Yang, the former presidential candidate and current CEO of mobile carrier Noble Moble, told CNN on Thursday that he had “met with the head of a lab” who had “a belief” that OpenAI’s Hugging Face hacker bots “have planted self-replicating code all over the internet, which makes the internet now unusable for the testing models.”

Yang said that this means that the real reason OpenAI and Anthropic have called for a slowdown is because “they have to create synthetic internets to train their bots, which is going to take some time and money.”

While there definitely is a trend towards using more synthetic data (aka, AI-generated data) for training models, an AI security professional told me that this particular safety issue is unlikely at best. Even if the internet is actually polluted with OpenAI’s Hugging Face hacker bots, AI researchers could simply filter out that code if they came upon it.

The second comment came from Noam Brown, who leads AI reasoning research at OpenAI. Speaking to Dwarkesh Patel on a podcast episode released on Thursday, Brown noted that the true take-away of the Hugging Face incident was that “people underestimated the AI.”

highlights.title: CA Gov. Gavin Newsom Signs Bill Addressing Catch in $750M Tax Credit for Hollywood
highlights.summary: The new law exempts indie projects from caps on the use of state tax credits and offers productions enhanced monetization of their incentives.
body: California Gov. Gavin Newsom on Friday signed into law a bill aimed at reducing Hollywood’s exposure to recent business tax credit caps legislation.

In a visit to Warner Bros. Studios the governor gave the green light to SB 186, which exempts independent productions from caps on the use of state tax credits that this year were not only extended, but also rendered permanent as of 2030.

SB 186 additionally offers new perks for productions that choose to monetize their tax credits instead of applying them to their annual tax bill: Productions can now monetize 95 percent of the credits instead of the previous 90 percent. Their payout timeline is also sped up to two years instead of the previous five.

It’s not a full exemption for Hollywood, but it’s a change that the industry pushed hard for. “Today’s action will maintain the state’s competitiveness so creators continue to make movies and shows in California — and keep bringing brilliant stories to life,” Motion Picture Association vp of state government affairs Arlen Valdivia said in a statement. “We thank Governor Newsom for his continued support for our industry’s health.”

body: Once you’ve started listening to Lizzy McAlpine, it’s hard to get her voice out of your head. The 26-year-old singer-songwriter started out by putting her music on SoundCloud during the early days of the COVID-19 pandemic, eventually going TikTok-viral with her 2022 single “Ceilings.” Now she’s collaborating with everyone from Noah Kahan to John Mayer and Finneas.

This week, Vogue spoke to McAlpine about the release of her folk-influenced fourth studio album, Angel; celebrating her 27th birthday and delving deep into Joni Mitchell’s back catalog; plus beginning to plan a couples costume for Halloween.

highlights.title: Does AI need an antitrust exemption so it doesn’t kill everyone????
highlights.summary: Today on Decoder, we’ve got the first of a two-part series on the future of business, and I’m talking with Jonathan Kanter, the former antitrust chief for the US Department of Justice in the Biden administration.
body: The biggest story in tech right now is the spiraling debate about AI safety and regulation. Researchers at the big AI labs including Anthropic and Google DeepMind have quit in noisy ways, saying the models pose real threats and safety isn’t being taken seriously across the industry. Other researchers have said the chance of AI killing us all is greater than 10 percent, and the CEOs of all these companies have issued various calls to slow down development and develop regulation, including asking for antitrust exemptions so they can all coordinate on safety issues.

That is a lot of ideas, and I am especially curious about the antitrust piece, which has led to accusations that these companies are seeking regulatory capture, attempting to form a cartel, and even somehow finding a way out from investor pressure ahead of their IPOs.

Jonathan brought huge antitrust cases against Google, Apple, and Ticketmaster during his time as antitrust chief, and along with Lina Khan, led what amounted to a full reboot of American antitrust policy. As you’ll hear him say, he won those cases against Google and Ticketmaster, and that case against Apple is still live in the Trump DOJ, surprising many.

highlights.title: The Sims 4's Next Update Will Make Your Sims Act a Lot More Naturally
highlights.summary: The next Sims 4 update is just around the corner, and it looks like it'll be a game-changer for Sims' autonomy. The official EA Laundry List for the next update lets us in on some of the changes being made this week, and its quality-of-life changes have certainly been a long time coming.
body: The update is focused on both gameplay additions and bug fixes. For example, the Gallery has often failed to load search result over the past few months, but the patch will finally tackle this matter. The team has improved game stability by reviewing player crash reports and tracking down the errors causing the issues. Hopefully, these updates can prevent similar problems in the future.

The main focus of the update is Sims' autonomy, as it aims to ensure that Sim behavior is as realistic as possible. The update will make it much more common for Sims to make eye contact during conversations. Instead of washing their hands in the kitchen sink after using the bathroom, Sims will finally use the sink closest to the toilet.

Speaking of going to the bathroom, Sims will walk faster when their Bladder Need is particularly low. As for those with a low Energy Need, they will actually sleep through the night rather than wake up to do random activities. Those may seem like small updates individually, but together they should give Sims much more realistic behaviors.

highlights.title: US fashion CEO resigns after physically restraining animal rights activists
highlights.summary: Steven Kolb of the Council of Fashion Designers of America was filmed during an altercation at New York fashion week. The chief executive of the Council of Fashion Designers of America, Steven Kolb, has resigned after he was filmed physically restraining two animal rights activists during an…
body: “After 20 years leading the CFDA, I have made the difficult decision to step down as CEO and president,” Kolb said in a statement. “I am enormously proud of what we have built together and believe this is the right moment for both me and the organisation to begin a new chapter.”
Kolb had been placed on leave on Tuesday pending a review of an incident during a COS show at New York fashion week on Sunday.

In a video, Kolb could be seen trying to restrain two People for the Ethical Treatment of Animals (Peta) protesters who attempted to disrupt the show in a demonstration against the use of wool by the H&M group, which owns COS.

Kolb pushed a protester, identified as Mason Melito, and covered his mouth. Kolb also wrestled a second protester to the ground, using his arms and a leg to restrain her and putting his hand over her mouth.

highlights.title: Google's Gemini AI hacked three companies in security test
highlights.summary: The AI model accessed the internet and guessed credentials to three websites, a Google official told the BBC.
body: Google's AI model Gemini autonomously hacked into three companies during a test of its cyber-security capabilities, the company has said, in what is thought to be the first known case of it carrying out such an act.
Gemini found "public information online and guessed credentials to access websites it thought were part of the test", a Google official told the BBC, noting that in each instance "the model stopped".
The affected companies were informed about the breaches, which happened in May.

It comes after renewed public scrutiny over the pace of AI development, as some tech firms calling for a slowdown over concerns over its potential threat to humanity - but not all companies or experts agree.

highlights.title: Star Wars Zero Company Unofficially Gets A Real Endgame
highlights.summary: Star Wars Zero Company is a fantastic strategy game, but it lacks a real endgame. Once you roll credits, you're simply encouraged to start a new save where you have some additional customization options and can recruit clone troopers from the start.
body: Cafiso's Aftermath DLC mod, which launched earlier in September but gained traction online this week, adds 1,000 more rotations (in-game days) to the strategy game. Once PC players roll credits, they can keep completing operations and missions, level up their characters, and earn more gear.

The mod doesn't simply increase the number of rotations at players' disposal, though. It also offers new enemy encounters and layers of progression to fill that added time. It added boss fights for Boba Fett, Palpatine, Gar Saxon, Rook Kast, Clone Commander, Purge Trooper, and Imperial Jet Trooper Commander, and turned Rex, Anakin, Cody, Baker, and Captain Crovo into recruitable characters. The player's Den Level cap has been raised to 15, while character bonds go up to +12 and focus trees now have 11 tiers.

On top of that, players can toggle an "Aftermath Threat" system that slightly increases enemies' health, shields, and damage after each encounter, and an "Aftermath Fatigue" system that debuffs operators if they are repeatedly used on back-to-back missions. It's quite impressive for an unofficial fan-made mod and is much more entertaining than simply starting a new playthrough.
points: Star Wars Zero Company is a fantastic strategy game, but it lacks a real endgame.

highlights.title: Miley’s ‘Bass Persuades’ Is Pretty and Passable, but Surprisingly Light on Bass… or Persuasion: Album Review
highlights.summary: The title track and first single from Miley Cyrus’ “Bass Persuades” was a classic act of misdirection, we now learn. Released two and a half weeks prior to the album, the song promised a tenth album full of bangers (with an S or Z, take your pick), mildly scolding the young people for not being
body: The core message of the album seems to be that things are going pretty well — make that extremely well — with fiancée Maxx Morando, who is a writer-producer collaborator on all but two of the tracks. Hearing Miley in a besotted state turns up mixed results. The third track, “Let’s Get Married,” is an abrupt left turn from the two bang-ier numbers that precede it into synthy easy listening/AC flavors, and what it delivers is not worth the whiplash; while it will probably be heard at some weddings to come, there may be a lot of attendees who would be itchy to please skip ahead to the vows.

Fortunately, that syrupy aside is a low point from which the album fairly quickly recovers. “Orbit,” next up, is just as romantic but one of the collection’s better tracks, as a power ballad — or even just ballad, without so much emphasis on the power — that applies some clever turns of phrase and thought to what could be a tired metaphor. Her significant other is the center of her solar system: “Place a marble on the floor / When you walk in the room, it’ll roll to you” is an image that makes for a lovely mash note.

highlights.title: The Black women who choose to have children on their own: ‘We’re going in eyes open’
highlights.summary: With growing support networks online and in person, these moms say they’re changing the narrative around Black single motherhood. When Chamise Alston was ready to have a child, she connected her computer to her TV and scrolled through profiles with her best friend, dismissing people who seemed like…
body: That winter day in 2023, Alston and her friend chose a donor who would help her become pregnant with her now 16-month-old daughter. As a Black woman, she felt empowered taking control of her reproductive destiny.
“I always wanted to be a mom,” said 40-year-old Alston. “Once I realized that there was a route for me to be a mom, sans a relationship, that’s always been my mission.”

Alston is part of a growing number of Black women opting to be single moms by choice (SMBC) through IVF, intrauterine insemination and adoption. Studies show that SMBCs are most likely to be financially stable, educated women in their late 30s. While Black women who choose solo parenting fit a similar profile as their white peers, they face unique challenges. Along with navigating stigmas around Black single motherhood, they also contend with a limited number of Black and brown sperm donors, and sometimes face discriminatory experiences from hospital staff during labor and delivery.

videos.title: NVIDIA Has GPUs If You Have Coin
videos.summary: GPU prices have become a meme, with NVIDIA leading the pack at (on average) 70% over listed MSRP for its consumer and gaming video cards. AMD and Intel are likewise running higher prices than previously, reaching new highs for GPU prices in our year-long series tracking them.
body: The best way to support our work is through our store:
points: GPU prices have become a meme, with NVIDIA leading the pack at (on average) 70% over listed MSRP for its consumer and gaming video cards.
AMD and Intel are likewise running higher prices than previously, reaching new highs for GPU prices in our year-long series tracking them.
November of 2025 seems like it was the best time to buy, with prices now climbing even past what we saw in February of 2026.
This continues to get worse with thanks to the ongoing DRAM availability crisis thanks to AI data center buildout -- one largely caused by the very companies that make the consumer GPUs.
